observed_product_semantics: writeAtomic() deliberately may leave a predecessor .bak-* after a committed canonical replacement when backup cleanup fails.
readState() falls back to readNewestBackup() whenever canonical parsing/read fails and returns that predecessor snapshot as ordinary authoritative state.

A predecessor backup from before markRunning can therefore contain pending while the newer canonical state had already durably recorded running and local tool side effects may subsequently have occurred.
If the canonical file later becomes unreadable, fallback returns pending and the runner may automatically execute the task again.

deterministic_probe.reproduction: valid pending predecessor backup + unreadable canonical => current readState recovers pending
deterministic_probe.candidate: backup recovery marks every non-done predecessor task uncertain/recoveredFromBackup and blocks automatic replay

required_fix_contract: Backup fallback must carry explicit provenance; it may not be indistinguishable from a clean canonical read.

Because the backup is a predecessor snapshot and the newer canonical transaction outcome is unknown once canonical bytes are unreadable, non-terminal recovered tasks must fail closed for automatic replay.

An already-done predecessor may remain resumable if its result is internally coherent; pending/running/failed/uncertain predecessor states require explicit recovery authorization or a stronger generation/commit proof.
Do not silently turn recovered pending/failed into runnable work.
Regression must model: predecessor pending -> canonical running committed -> possible side effect -> canonical corruption -> backup fallback; automatic executor count must stay zero after restart.
This rule should be composed with the store-wide interprocess serialization and status-transition guard findings; they solve different failure modes.
